title: Any recommendations for Steam deals under €10?
author: No-Zookeepergame8837
selftext:
Hi! After buying some games on sale, I'm left with €15 in my account. Ideally, I'd like to keep €5 in case another sale comes up that interests me (although I wouldn't mind spending it here if it's for a really good game). So I was wondering, do you have any pro-AI recommendations for games under €10? Importantly, I'm absolutely not interested in ANYTHING from anti-AI developers. I don't support any kind of terrorism, without exception, which is one of the reasons I'm asking here. I'd prefer games that use AI (But is fine if the game doesn't use it, as long as the dev isn't anti-AI.) . My only requirements are:



\- That they're not just basic puzzle games where you just move puzzle pieces around.



\- Survivor games only if they bring some new mechanics to the genre, not just reskins of the other 90 that already exist.



\- That they're in Spanish or English.



\- It must have real gameplay (Like, not visual novels or clicker games for example).



\- No hyper-realistic graphics.





Aside from that, any game is fine by me, although my main preferences (not mandatory, just what I prefer, but I'm open to anything, even if it's not on this list) right now would be:



\- No DLC or only cosmetic DLC (I hate feeling like I'm not getting the full experience...)



\- Easily moddable (I just like to add my own "mental canon," lol. I don't know, I always tend to mod what I play to add characters from other games, change conversations, endings, etc. I don't publish it or anything, so I don't really care if it is compatible with the workshop, just being able to modify it is enough.)



\- Creature collector games (I just want one. I've already played Siralim Ultimate, which is the only one I know that uses AI for translations, but I'm looking for something more "pure creature collector," like, without fusion mechanics, with a clear level cap and completion of its equivalent to the Pokédex, etc.)



\- Not 3D (I prefer 2D games, especially pixel art)



\-Made in RPG Maker (Not just because they're the easiest to mod, it's simply that I like RPG Maker "semi-rigid" mechanics, like baitable enemies, triggers in stacks that you can manipulate as you please, etc. In general I love to fully exploit unexpected mechanics in videogames, and RPG Maker, especially MV and VX ACE, is by far the engine I have the most experience exploiting. They don't have to be glitches that strictly give advantages, I simply like to see the game break in unexpected ways, like, for example, in Skyrim, simply walking through walls with a plate and getting stuck or falling off the most of the time. Aside from the 4-5 reachable vendor chests, it doesn't really have any practical use for a normal playthrough, but I simply love doing it.)



As I said, none of this is mandatory, just things I currently prefer.

comments.body: This post is not specific to AI based game development. See rule #1.
